payload.summary: Fix mean([]) so it raises ValueError instead of crashing with ZeroDivisionError by adding an explicit empty-sequence guard in stats.mean before performing the division.

tasks.title: Add empty-sequence guard to mean()
tasks.description: In stats.py, modify mean(values) to raise ValueError when the input sequence is empty. The guard must occur before sum(values) / len(values) so mean([]) raises ValueError with a clear message (e.g., 'mean of empty sequence is not defined'). Do not change behavior for non-empty sequences, and keep median() and total() unchanged.

tasks.title: Run tests and verify mean([]) raises ValueError
tasks.description: Run the test suite (tests/test_calc.py) to confirm test_mean_empty now passes and all existing tests still pass. Verify mean([]) raises ValueError and mean([2,4,6]) still equals 4.0.

findings: stats.py:mean(values) computes sum(values) / len(values) with no empty-sequence guard. Calling mean([]) therefore raises ZeroDivisionError (0 / 0) rather than the documented/expected ValueError.
tests/test_calc.py already contains test_mean_empty (lines 35-38) which asserts pytest.raises(ValueError) for mean([]), so the fix should make that test pass without changing other behavior.
calc.py:divide() provides a pattern for the guard style used in this repo: raise ValueError with a clear message before the operation.

changes: Added empty-sequence guard in stats.mean() to raise ValueError before division

payload.summary: Ran python3 -m pytest tests/test_calc.py -q: 10 passed. Verified mean([]) raises ValueError('mean of empty sequence is not defined') and mean([2,4,6]) == 4.0. Lint/syntax check passed with no output.

suggestions: Guard uses len(values) == 0, which is explicit and correct for sequences; no change needed.
